Provenance.description:
Where an observation came from: an artifact and, optionally, a span.
Extracted claims carry the artifact's id; a sender that ingests a
document and structured claims about it in the same pipeline does not
know the id yet, so it may cite the document by its own `event_id`
instead — resolved to `artifact_id` at ingest (D-039). The document
must land first (same batch is fine: documents are stored before the
batch's claims); an unresolvable reference rejects the claim.

ScopeSpec.description:
The set of entities a question is about — several computers, or an
anchor plus everything related to it ("domain X and its contents").

`expand` names the containment/relational predicates to follow outward
from the subjects (e.g. ["member_of"]); `depth` bounds the traversal.

subjects.description: anchors of the scope; bounded so one request cannot name a whole namespace (expansion is how a scope grows, D-046)
subjects.title: Subjects

siblings.description: also turn back along the same predicate at a reached entity — user -member_of-> group <-member_of- every other member. Off by default: through a group that holds every user it pulls the whole directory into the scope (D-080)
siblings.title: Siblings

follow_extracted.description: also traverse edges that were extracted from documents (D-023 second-class witnesses); off by default so a hostile document cannot rewrite the topology a scope walks (D-046)
follow_extracted.title: Follow Extracted

ScopeSpec.title: ScopeSpec

AskRequest.description:
Two time axes (docs/architecture.md, D-024/D-046): `as_of` = what did
we KNOW at T, measured on observation time (`observed_at <= as_of`:
when the source asserted it), the closest proxy to knowledge time for
backfilled corpora, where `recorded_at` is load day; `recorded_at`
remains the audit column. `valid_at` = what was TRUE at T (fact time —
only observations whose validity window covers T survive, and facts
with no window at all are kept). A fact scheduled for after T but
asserted before it is part of the `as_of` view; hiding it is
`valid_at`'s job.

budget.description: token budget; mandatory cap (LOOMCTX_MAX_BUDGET is the real ceiling)
budget.title: Budget

or a span of a stored document (excerpts). At least one of

Citation.title: Citation

ContextItem.description:
Every item is cited (hard constraint 3): facts and conflicts cite

ExpansionHandle.description:
Opaque 'there is more here' pointer; feed back to expand().
kind says what was left out: more observations of one predicate, or a
whole conflict that didn't fit the budget (never silently dropped).
ExpansionHandle.title: ExpansionHandle

ScopeTruncation.description:
Partial coverage a reader must know about. An entity whose
observations exceeded the gather limit: only the newest `gathered` of
`total` were examined. A reader must not conclude absence about it —
"no KEV fact among the kernel's CVEs" means nothing when 1,740 of 2,740
were never looked at (D-038). A scope walk cut by the entity cap is
reported the same way, with reason `scope_cap` (D-058).

reason.description: gather_limit: only the newest `gathered` of the `total` observations about `entity` that this caller may see were examined (D-038). scope_cap: the scope walk stopped at the entity cap (LOOMCTX_MAX_SCOPE_ENTITIES / LOOMCTX_MAX_SCOPE_OBSERVATIONS) while expanding `entity` — `gathered` entities are in the pack of at least `total` reached (D-058). max_paths: a path search found more connecting paths to `entity` (the `to` endpoint) than were returned — `gathered` of at least `total` (the cap, or the token budget, cut the rest, D-067). depth: the search reached the depth cap while the frontier still had unexplored entities, so a longer path may exist (D-067)
reason.title: Reason

ScopeTruncation.title: ScopeTruncation

ContextPack.description: The unit of retrieval: budgeted, ranked, cited, expandable.

omitted_handles.description: expansion threads that existed beyond the handle cap; narrow the scope or raise the budget to see them (D-035)
omitted_handles.title: Omitted Handles

truncated.description: entities whose observations exceeded the gather limit: coverage is partial there, so absence cannot be concluded (D-038)
truncated.title: Truncated

charged_tokens.description: what the pack charged against `budget`, in its compact rendered form: every item's text plus its citations, and every handle's hint plus id. At most `budget`, with one exception: the first handle always ships (a pack that cut something must say so): when facts cannot be trimmed to make room for it — the budget is under two handles, or conflicts, briefs and excerpts filled it — charged_tokens exceeds `budget` by at most that one handle's cost (D-051, D-058)
charged_tokens.title: Charged Tokens

withheld_briefs.description: entity briefs (dossiers) that exist but were left out: a brief is prose written from every observation it cites, so a type-scoped caller gets it only when it may see all of them, and a brief never takes more than a quarter of the budget (D-058)
withheld_briefs.title: Withheld Briefs

notes.description: what the pack could not do as asked, and what it did instead: an expand predicate the namespace does not know (with the closest ones it does), an attribute named in expand taken as the question's topic rather than walked, a subject that names no entity. Advice about the request, not evidence: not cited, not charged against the budget (D-064)
notes.title: Notes

PathRequest.description:
"What connects A to B?" — enumerate the edge sequence(s) that already
exist in the data between two entities along the named predicates (D-067).
Domain-agnostic (the KEV host -> product -> cve chain, the AD user ->
group -> domain chain alike). It reports paths that EXIST; it does not
rank, score, or weight edges by exploitability, and emits no such advice.
`as_of` / `valid_at` carry the two time axes of AskRequest.

from.description: the entity the path starts at (serialized as 'from')

via.description: predicates to traverse (both directions where the edge is naturally reversible, mirroring the scope walk); empty = the namespace's registered containment predicates, like a scope
via.title: Via

depth.description: the most edges a path may hold; clamped to the path depth cap (6) and noted when a longer one is asked
depth.title: Depth

siblings.description: also allow a path to turn back along the same predicate at an entity — user -member_of-> group <-member_of- admin: a shared group, not a route. Off by default, as in a scope walk (D-080)
siblings.title: Siblings

max_paths.description: the most paths to return, shortest first; more found than this is reported in `truncated` (reason max_paths)
max_paths.title: Max Paths

budget.description: token budget, charged on the rendered path text plus citations exactly as a pack is (LOOMCTX_MAX_BUDGET is the ceiling)
budget.title: Budget

PathEdge.description:

observation's `subject` `predicate` `object`, cited and time-scoped. The
traversal direction is implied by the edge's place in the sequence — an
`affects` edge (cve -> product) walked product -> cve still renders
cve affects product, so the reader sees the fact as recorded (D-067).

PathPack.description:
The connecting edge sequences a PathRequest found, shortest first. Each
edge is cited (hard constraint 3) and time-scoped; a superseded edge
(D-050) never appears and `as_of` / `valid_at` filter every edge. `notes`
carry the same request advice a pack does (D-064): an unknown `via`
predicate with close matches, an unknown from/to entity, "no path found
within depth N", a `to` a longer depth might reach.

charged_tokens.description: what the returned paths charged against `budget`: every edge's rendered text plus its citation, summed (D-067)
charged_tokens.title: Charged Tokens

truncated.description: what the search could not fully return: a hub whose edges the gather cap only partly examined (gather_limit), the walk cut at the entity/observation cap (scope_cap), more paths than max_paths or the budget allowed (max_paths), or the depth cap reached with the frontier still open (depth)
truncated.title: Truncated

node_status.description: for every entity on a returned path, its current value of each predicate the registry marks `node_status` (an account's `enabled`, say), cited and charged against the budget: a path through a disabled account is returned, and says so (D-080)
node_status.title: Node Status

ListFilter.description:
One condition on an entity's CURRENT value of a predicate: the newest
visible, unsuperseded, in-scope row (valid at `valid_at` when one is
asked), compared case-insensitively on scalars. `ne` holds for an entity
with no value on record (D-107: "accounts not disabled" includes the
ones whose status was never collected — the page says how many).

predicate.description: the predicate compared; for within / not_within, the edge predicates walked, comma-separated for any mix of them (D-116): 'has_ace,member_of' within computer:X holds for every account with rights over X, directly or through its groups
predicate.title: Predicate

value.description: the compared value: a scalar for eq / ne / contains, a list for in; an entity ('type:key') for within / not_within; ignored by exists / absent
value.title: Value

depth.description: within / not_within: the most `predicate` edges from the entity to `value` (nested membership: user -member_of-> group -member_of-> … -> value); clamped to the list depth cap
depth.title: Depth

ListFilter.title: ListFilter

ListRequest.description:
"Which entities ...?" — an exact, paged set of entities instead of a
ranked pack (D-107). The candidates are the entities that reach `of`
along `via` within `depth` edges (group membership, nested), or, without
`of`, every entity of `type`; `where` filters them, all conditions
holding. Every row is cited by the rows that admitted it; the total is
exact unless a cap is noted.

type.description: keep only entities of this type (user, computer, host…)
type.title: Type

of.description: list entities connected to this one (a group's members, a host's software) instead of a whole type

via.description: the edge predicates walked from `of`; empty = the namespace's registered containment predicates
via.title: Via

direction.description: in: entities whose edge points AT `of` (members of a group: user member_of group); out: what `of` points at; any: both
direction.title: Direction

depth.description: the most edges between a listed entity and `of` (nested membership); clamped to 6 and noted
depth.title: Depth

paths.description: an `of` listing: give each row its route to `of`, every edge cited (how an account reaches a machine through groups and ACL grants); costs budget
paths.title: Paths

fields.description: predicates whose current value each row should show, cited (beyond the ones `where` already names)
fields.title: Fields

budget.description: token budget, charged on each row's rendered text plus its citations; rows past it are left for the next page
budget.title: Budget

SemanticMatch.description:
An entity surfaced by meaning rather than by name (D-025): the best
matching fact is the evidence, cited like any pack item.
SemanticMatch.title: SemanticMatch

aliases.description: other names a question or an agent uses for this type (an LDAP 'computer' is a 'machine' or 'workstation', a 'user' an 'account'): a request naming an alias that is not itself a registered type reads it as this type, with a note (D-116)
aliases.title: Aliases

NotCollectedDef.description:
Something a namespace's sources do not carry, declared by the
connector (D-110): an LDAP export has no local group membership, so
"local admins of WS-1" cannot be answered from it — and an empty result
must not read as "none". `words` are the plain terms a question uses for
it; the engine notes the declaration when a question names them.

mistaken_for.description: predicates whose facts are commonly taken for this gap (an LDAP export's has_ace, rights over the directory object, read as local admin): a result carrying them notes the difference (D-116)
mistaken_for.title: Mistaken For

NotCollectedDef.title: NotCollectedDef

object_types.description: allowed object entity types; empty = any entity or scalar
object_types.title: Object Types

containment.description: a 'contains / member of' relation: scopes with no explicit `expand` follow every containment predicate (D-012/D-024)
containment.title: Containment

node_status.description: a scalar that qualifies an entity as a step on a path (an account's `enabled`): find_path reports each path entity's current value of it, cited (D-080)
node_status.title: Node Status

label.description: a scalar that names its subject (a sAMAccountName, displayName, UPN, login): entity search matches its values as well as keys, so an entity keyed by an opaque id (a SID, a GUID) can be found by name (D-091)
label.title: Label

aliases.description: the source's own attribute names and plain words for this predicate (servicePrincipalName, sAMAccountName, operatingSystem): a request naming one that is not itself a registered predicate reads it as this predicate, with a note (D-116)
aliases.title: Aliases

display.description: the label a pack shows beside its subject's opaque key, over the namespace's other labels: a name that says where the entity lives (`dlee@dev.local`, a UPN) rather than a bare login that reads the same in every domain (D-097)
display.title: Display

QueryDef.description:
A named, parameterized question a namespace answers exactly (D-108):
a ListRequest template whose string values may be `{param}`
placeholders — "effective_members(group)", "unconstrained delegation
hosts that are not DCs". Data, not code: a connector registers the
questions its domain asks, and an agent runs one by name instead of
composing the walk and filters itself. `namespace`, paging and budget
come from the call, never the template.

request.description: a ListRequest without namespace / limit / offset / budget / as_of / valid_at; '{param}' strings are substituted
request.title: Request

QueryDef.title: QueryDef

QueryParam.description:
One parameter of a named query (D-108). Without a default it is
required. An `entity` parameter takes a 'type:key' handle or a name the
namespace's label predicates know (resolved like find_entity, within
`entity_type` when set).
QueryParam.title: QueryParam

SchemaRegistration.description:
Per-namespace registry (D-024). Registering is additive (a later POST
merges by name). Validation on ingest: a registered predicate's
object_types are always enforced; with `strict` the namespace also
rejects unregistered predicates and entity types.

queries.description: named questions the namespace answers exactly (D-108); a later registration replaces a query of the same name
queries.title: Queries

not_collected.description: what the namespace's sources do not carry (D-110); merged by topic
not_collected.title: Not Collected

SchemaRegistration.title: SchemaRegistration

IngestItemResult.description:
Outcome of one envelope in a batch (D-034). `rejected` items carry
the reason; the rest of the batch still lands — a shipper's bad record
never blocks its good ones.
IngestItemResult.title: IngestItemResult
